description:
## Finding

`ChatBackend::expire_message`'s rustdoc has an "Idempotency"
section (`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:856-866`) saying:

```
/// If the message no longer exists (already expired or deleted),
/// this method SHOULD return `Ok(())` rather than
/// `BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::NotFound)`.
```

The rustdoc is silent on the **state-token side effect** of the
SHOULD-Ok-on-missing-id case. The integration test asserts the
state token MUST NOT bump:

`crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:1664-1672`:

```rust
let state_after: jmap_types::State = backend
    .get_state::<jmap_chat_types::Message>(&(), &account_id)
    .await
    .expect("get_state");
assert_eq!(
    state_after.as_ref(),
    "0",
    "expire_message on missing id must not bump the state counter"
);
```

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A natural-minimal implementation interprets "SHOULD return Ok(())"
as "treat the no-op as a successful write" and:

1. Increments the `Message` type state token (because that's what
   `update_object` / `destroy_object` do on every successful op).
2. Returns `Ok(())`.

This passes the rustdoc contract verbatim (it returns `Ok(())`)
but breaks Message/changes subscribers: every retried expiry
call against an already-expired-or-deleted message produces a
spurious `Message/changes` delta with no records. A buggy
expiry scheduler that retries on transient errors and races with
itself triggers a state-bump storm; subscribers re-poll and
re-poll, getting empty change sets each time.

## Recommendation

Tighten the Idempotency wording. Replace:

```
/// If the message no longer exists (already expired or deleted),
/// this method SHOULD return `Ok(())` rather than
/// `BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::NotFound)`.
```

with:

```
/// If the message no longer exists (already expired or deleted),
/// this method SHOULD return `Ok(())` rather than
/// `BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::NotFound)`, AND MUST
/// NOT bump the `Message` type state token in that case. The
/// no-op case must be observationally indistinguishable from
/// "the scheduler never fired" for `Message/changes`
/// subscribers.
```

## Engineering basis

- Test assertion at `integration.rs:1664-1672` verbatim.
- Rustdoc at `backend.rs:856-866` verbatim.
- Reference impl behaviour: `memory.rs` `expire_message` returns
  early without state bump on missing id (else the test would
  fail).

## Priority justification

P3 — the contract is implicit in "idempotent" but a careful
implementer rightly questions whether "successfully no-opped" is
"successful" in the state-bump sense. The 4-word fix
("AND MUST NOT bump") closes the ambiguity. Not P2 because the
failure mode is bandwidth waste (spurious state bumps), not
correctness drift.
title: API contract: expire_message rustdoc says SHOULD return Ok(()) on missing id but is silent on whether state token must NOT bump in that case
